analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, Yahweh speaks, and אֶל introduces Abram as the person he addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, “Yahweh said to Abram,” אֶל introduces Abram as the addressee. The masculine singular command לֶךְ, “go,” is directed to him. Haqor files the name under אבה through its אָב (“father”) element.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: YHWH commands Abram to go from his land (מֵאַרְצְךָ) to the land he will show him (אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ).
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram. The following לְךָ is a separate word.

draft.change: Add Genesis 12:1 as an example of the existing Hebrew sense le-dative.
draft.definition: With a suffix referring back to the subject, לְ can mark the subject’s personal involvement in the action.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 12:1 the subject of לֶךְ and the suffix of לְךָ both refer to Abram. The command tells him to leave his country, his kindred and his father’s house.

analysis.evidence: In לֶךְ לְךָ, Yahweh tells Abram to go. The suffix on לְךָ refers to Abram himself, giving the phrase the force of “go your way.” The destination is expressed separately by אֶל הָאָרֶץ, “to the land.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition לְ with the second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ךָ, referring to Abram.
analysis.sense: Dative of personal interest. The suffix refers back to the person commanded to go.

analysis.evidence: The command לֶךְ tells Abram to leave his country, his kindred, and his father’s house. The contrast with אֶל הָאָרֶץ ‘to the land’ identifies his country as the territory he is leaving.
analysis.morphology: מֵ is the prefixed form of מִן ‘from’. אַרְצְ is the singular construct form of the common-gender noun אֶרֶץ, and ךָ is the second-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: Abram is told to leave ‘your land’, ‘your kindred’, and ‘your father’s house’. The sequence narrows from his country through his wider circle of relatives to his paternal household.
analysis.morphology: וּ means ‘and’. מִ is the preposition מִן ‘from’, whose nun assimilates to the following mem. The feminine singular noun is in construct with ךָ, the second-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ, “and from your father’s house,” בֵּית supplies “house,” and אָבִיךָ identifies whose house Abram is to leave.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: After the command לֶךְ ‘go’, מֵאַרְצְךָ ‘from your land’ identifies Abram’s point of departure, and אֶל הָאָרֶץ ‘to the land’ identifies his destination.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶל marks the land as Abram’s destination, and אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ identifies it as the land YHWH will show him. The earlier מֵאַרְצְךָ names the country he is to leave.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause modifying הָאָרֶץ, “the land that I will show you.” The land is what Yahweh will show, and the suffix on אַרְאֶךָּ refers to Abram.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ, the land is what Yahweh will show, and the suffix identifies Abram as the one who will see it.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, first person common singular, with a second person masculine singular pronominal suffix referring to Abram.
